meaning: of Beauchamp
author_comment: Mr. Lower mentions a Beauchamp near Avranches, and another near Havre. Its equivalent local term in England is Fairfield. Hugh de Bel-Champ, or Beauchamp (latinized in early records as 'de Bello-Campo'), obtained forty-three lordships from the Conqueror (Lower). headword: Beaumont, Beaman, Beament, Beamont, Beman, Bemand, Bement
meaning: de Belmont or de Beaumont
author_comment: 'Roger de Belmont appears in Domesday as a chief tenant in cos. Gloucester and Dorset' (Lower), probably a near kinsman of the Conqueror. 'The Itin. de la Normandie gives five places in that Province called Beaumont' (ibid.). Nearer home are parishes or places named Beaumont in cos. Cumb., Essex, and Leicester (ibid.). Generally speaking, the surname is of Norman extraction; v. Beaman.
source: Testa de Nevill, sive Liber Feodorum, temp. Hen. III-Edw. I
record_text: Mathaeus de Bello Monte, co. Devon, Hen. III-Edw. I. K.
